bds.h: Federal appeals court clears way for U.S. army to detonate degraded bomb-making material in Iowa
bds.lede: U.S. President Donald Trump on Monday halted the planned detonation of several tons of degraded bomb-making material at an Iowa ammunition plant, urging a federal appeals court to first sign off on what he called the safest way to handle the situation.
rows: A federal appeals court on Monday declined to block the Army from detonating explosives containing lead azide at a munitions plant in Iowa.

U.S. President Donald Trump on Monday halted the planned detonation of several tons of degraded bomb-making material at an Iowa ammunition plant, urging a federal appeals court to first sign off on what he called the safest way to handle the situation.

A federal appeals court on Monday cleared the way for the U.S. Army to detonate several tons of degraded bomb-making material at an Iowa ammunition plant, finding that the plan should adequately limit the dispersal of lead dust into the atmosphere.
President Trump has further postponed the US Army’s planned detonation of nearly five tonnes of lead azide in Iowa.
Trump said he wants the OK from the federal appeals court and incoming Iowa governor to proceed.

The U.S. Army's controlled detonation of 68 barrels of unstable lead azide in Iowa on Wednesday is expected to produce a plume of dust containing lead particles that could extend as far as 100 miles away, a plan that residents, lawmakers and environmental groups say was not communicated…
